### Bisque (Paramount / TheSkyX)

Devices: Telescope.

Protocol documentation: `AlpacaCore/external/Bisque/` (INDI reference driver and TheSkyX scripting API docs). No external SDK required — communicates via JavaScript commands over TCP to TheSkyX Pro.

Connection types: TCP only. TheSkyX acts as middleware between the driver and the actual mount hardware.

- Communication is via JavaScript command snippets sent to the TheSkyX TCP scripting server (default port 3040).
- Commands are strings terminated with `#`. Responses are prefixed with `|No error. Error = 0.` on success, terminated with `#`.
- Special case: Handshake (`ConnectAndDoNotUnpark`/`IsConnected`) returns just `1` with no prefix.
- Slew is async: set `sky6RASCOMTele.Asynchronous = true`, call `SlewToRaDec`, poll `IsSlewComplete`.
- Pulse guiding uses `sky6DirectGuide.MoveTelescope(dRA, dDec)` with arcsecond displacement. `sky6DirectGuide.lAsynchronous=0` makes that call wait for completion; keep it on a joinable driver worker so `PulseGuide()` returns promptly while `IsPulseGuiding` remains observable.
- Open loop motion for MoveAxis uses `DoCommand(9, 'direction|rate')` and `DoCommand(10, '')`.
- Park uses `ParkAndDoNotDisconnect()` to keep TCP connection alive (not `Park()` which disconnects).
- Pier side is read-only via `DoCommand(11, 'Pier Side')` — returns 1 for west of pier, else east.
- Find Home uses `FindHome()` with a 60-second timeout.
- Slew speed presets: 9 rates (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 32x, 64x, 128x, 256x, 512x sidereal).
- UTCDate's source is the **TheSkyX computer**, never the bridge: Software Bisque's [Paramount ME II and MX User Guide](https://www.physics.muni.cz/~glos/Paramount/Paramount%20ME%20II%20and%20MX%20User%20Guide.pdf), pp. 27–29, requires Use Computer Clock and identifies that clock as the source for mount initialization and LST. [Script TheSky 1.32](https://www.bisque.com/wp-content/scriptthesky/index.html) executes ECMA-262 JavaScript remotely; `new Date().getTime()` supplies UTC milliseconds without timezone/DST conversion. In the same script, [DocumentProperty(5)/DocPropOut](https://www.bisque.com/wp-content/scriptthesky/classsky6_star_chart.html) must confirm UseComputerClock (nonzero). Manual/chart-time mode returns `InvalidOperation`; chart JD is not substituted. No script changes the clock mode, site, timezone or DST. Writes raise `PropertyNotImplemented` after connection/link checks: setting chart time is not setting the operating-system clock.
- The Script TheSky 1.32 `sky6StarChart::Sk6DocumentProperty` enum explicitly declares `sk6DocProp_UseComputerClock = 5`; its enumerator description says "Zero if not using the computers clock non-zero otherwise." See the [class reference](https://www.bisque.com/wp-content/scriptthesky/classsky6_star_chart.html), verified 2026-10-29. The fake does not establish this vendor fact.
- UTC is seeded at connect and refreshed by the existing status sample, with `UtcOffset` in the frame to advance remote UTC by task-clock elapsed time between replies. A failed time query retains the established anchor and records its diagnostic; without an anchor the getter raises that error. Explicit unavailable/manual mode clears the anchor. A later good reply re-anchors time. Snapshot resets and publication tokens prevent cross-session reuse. Stale alone does not refuse UTC; existing link fault/loss checks still apply. Evidence is fake-only (`[bisque][utcdate]`); actual TheSkyX script execution and hardware timing are not validated by the fake.
- Every TheSkyX exchange (connect and handshake, FindHome, Park and its polls, slews and their completion polls, sync, `SetTracking`, MoveAxis, Unpark, SetPark, the position samples at the end of sync, slew complete, FindHome and Park) runs with the driver `mutex_` free, under the protocol wrapper's per-link lock (the wrapper is one instance per process, so that lock is the I/O lock); `mutex_` stays the short state lock. MoveAxis, both slew forms and AbortSlew hold `initiator_mutex_` across gate, command and state write (a sync slew drops it before its wait); Park holds it across its gate and the Park send only, sets `parking_` before it lets go, and runs the IsParked poll without it, so a slew during the poll is refused like a parked mount and AbortSlew never waits for the poll (AbortSlew, Unpark and a disconnect clear `parking_`; `park_epoch_` keeps a stale Park's exit from clearing a newer Park's flag); both slew forms re-check Connected and park after the live IsTracking read; order `initiator_mutex_`, then the wrapper's lock, then `mutex_` (leaf). A control-path end takes the snapshot token under `mutex_`, samples without it and publishes under it, so a write since drops the publish (`publish_measurement()`). Connect runs under `transition_mutex_`; `set_connected(false)` clears state, releases `mutex_`, then closes the transport. Getters never wait behind the wire ([decision 0016](../../docs/decisions/0016-getters-never-wait-on-device-io.md)). Tests: the timing cases in `test_bisque_telescope_snapshot.cpp` (FindHome, SyncToCoordinates position read, `SetTracking`, the connect's IsParked query, Park's IsParked poll, a disconnect behind a PulseGuide reply, the sync slew's IsSlewComplete poll, the MoveAxis, SlewToCoordinatesAsync, Unpark and SetPark commands).
